title: UX project setup interview
intro: Answer what you know. Add a note when an option does not fit. The agent will keep unknowns as open questions.

categories.title: Product
categories.intro: Define the product and its language.

questions.label: What is the product name?
questions.explanation: This name appears in the project UX file and its generated README.

questions.label: What does the product help people do?
questions.explanation: Describe the main user outcome in one or two sentences. Do not describe only the technology.

questions.label: What product locale should guide interface copy?
questions.explanation: Use a locale such as en-GB or nl-NL. This controls product labels, not the report language.

categories.title: Customers
categories.intro: Describe the people, situations, and problems that shape the experience.

questions.label: Which customer roles use or receive this product?
questions.explanation: Give role labels, such as first-time shop owner or account administrator. Avoid unsupported names or demographic details.

questions.label: How many important customer types should we model first?
questions.explanation: A small number keeps the first project file useful. Add a note if roles overlap.

questions.label: What are these customers trying to achieve?
questions.explanation: Describe the job and the desired outcome. Separate the outcome from the feature they requested.

questions.label: When and where do they use the product?
questions.explanation: Include the trigger, setting, time pressure, interruptions, and information available at that moment.

questions.label: How much product or domain knowledge do they usually have?
questions.explanation: This guides labels, explanations, defaults, and recovery help.

questions.label: Which devices do customers use?
questions.explanation: Select known devices. Add a note about shared devices, poor connections, or unusual input methods.

questions.label: What frustrates customers during the task?
questions.explanation: List observed problems or clearly mark guesses. Do not present an agent assumption as user evidence.

questions.label: What might make them stop, leave, or ask for help?
questions.explanation: Include confusing steps, missing information, cost, trust concerns, and recovery failures when known.

categories.title: Evidence
categories.intro: Separate real product evidence from assumptions. Add a note when evidence covers only one segment.

questions.label: What real user or product evidence is available?
questions.explanation: Choose every source that exists. Public web material is not evidence about this product's users.

questions.label: Where can the agent find the available evidence?
questions.explanation: Give safe file paths, source IDs, or a short description. Do not paste secrets or personal data.

questions.label: What groups and questions do the interviews cover?
questions.explanation: This prevents a small interview sample from being treated as evidence about every customer.

questions.label: What events, period, and segments do the analytics cover?
questions.explanation: A metric needs a definition, time period, and segment before it can support a user claim.

categories.title: Tone
categories.intro: Set the voice for product copy.

questions.label: How should the product sound?
questions.explanation: Describe the voice with practical words, such as calm, direct, or encouraging.

questions.label: Which words should the product use or avoid?
questions.explanation: List preferred terms, banned terms, and domain terms that need plain-language explanations.

questions.label: Which accessibility target should guide the work?
questions.explanation: WCAG 2.2 AA is the default. Choose another target only when the project requires it.

questions.label: Which screen sizes must the team check?
questions.explanation: The default checks are phone 390×844, tablet 820×1180, laptop 1440×900, and wide 1920×1080. Add a note for more sizes.

questions.label: What design system source should the agent use?
questions.explanation: Choose the source that exists in the project. The agent reads it and does not create or rewrite it.

questions.label: What is the design system path?
questions.explanation: Give a repository-relative path. Leave this empty when no design system exists.

questions.label: What are the three most important customer tasks?
questions.explanation: Name each task and its observable success outcome. Record fewer tasks when the product is small.
